title: Insulin Tolerance Test in Mouse
author: Nancy Smith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wxjffkn
materials: Return food and environmental enrichments to cages.

steps.title: Prepare insulin stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make Stock 1 by mixing 50 µL of 100 U/mL Humulin R with 4 950 µL cold sterile 1× PBS; invert 3–4 times. Then make Stock 2 by diluting 1 mL of Stock 1 into 9 mL cold sterile 1× PBS; invert 3–4 times and keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Fast mice and set up cages
steps.instruction: Begin fasting at ~09:00 am; fast each mouse for 4–6 h. Transfer mice to a clean cage with a wire top, keep water bottles available, save any High‑Fat‑Diet food for return after the test, and mark each tail with a Sharpie for identification.

steps.title: Weigh mice and calculate insulin dose
steps.instruction: Weigh each mouse, record body weight, and calculate the insulin bolus: 1–1.2 U/kg (use 1 U/kg for calculation: weight (g) × 10 = µL of insulin Stock 2). Record the volume in the ITT‑template spreadsheet.

steps.title: Prepare syringes with insulin
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 26‑G needle, draw the calculated volume of insulin Stock 2 for each mouse, load the syringes, and place them in front of the home cage.

steps.title: Measure baseline blood glucose
steps.instruction: Restrain the mouse, clean the tail with 70 % ethanol and gauze, prick the tail vein, collect a drop of blood onto a OneTouch Ultra strip, and read glucose with the OneTouch Ultra 2 meter to obtain the time‑zero value.

steps.title: Inject insulin intraperitoneally
steps.instruction: Restrain the mouse, place it in dorsal recumbency with head down, locate the injection site halfway between the ventral midline and lateral side at the natural bend of the knee, insert the needle at a 30–45° angle into the left or right lower abdominal quadrant, aspirate to confirm no blood, intestine or bladder entry (air bubble only), inject the insulin dose, and return the mouse to its cage.

steps.title: Start timing post‑injection
steps.instruction: Begin the experimental timer at the moment the insulin injection is completed.

steps.title: Collect and record glucose at intervals
steps.instruction: At 15, 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes after injection, restrain each mouse, obtain a tail‑blood sample as in step 5, read glucose, and record each value on the Insulin Tolerance Test record sheet (template referenced in step 2), noting the animal’s condition throughout.
